request: We should know which of our contacts are most influential so we can prioritize them.
executive_summary: This release will implement a contact prioritization feature that allows users to categorize contacts based on their influence levels with specified permissions and guidelines. Automated influence determination, external integrations, and changes to existing user permissions are not included in this release. Human decision-makers must ensure that the approval processes for permissions are adequately managed to prevent unauthorized changes.

core_commitments.text: Enable users to categorize contacts based on their influence level.
Provide users with a visual representation of contact influence levels for prioritization.

in_scope.text: Create a new field in the contact record called 'Influence Level' that allows designated users (regional coordinators and project managers with approved permissions) to assign a value (e.g., Low, Medium, High) to each contact.
in_scope.note: A new field for 'Influence Level' was created to allow designated users to assign values, addressing the need for a systematic way to categorize influence.

in_scope.text: Develop a simple interface for regional coordinators and project managers with approved permissions to update the Influence Level of contacts, accompanied by a review mechanism where a designated administrator checks for consistency and correctness of updates.
in_scope.note: A simple interface for updating 'Influence Level' has been established, including a review mechanism, ensuring accuracy and consistency in data.

in_scope.text: Implement a filter in the contacts list that allows users to sort contacts by Influence Level.
Add tooltips or help text with standardized guidelines outlining specific criteria and examples for determining Influence Level for contacts.
in_scope.note: Standardized guidelines have been established to accompany tooltips, ensuring consistent categorization among users.

in_scope.text: Include a process for auditing 'Influence Level' data retention, ensuring that sensitive categorizations are reviewed annually and retained only as long as necessary for operational needs.
in_scope.note: A data retention auditing process was instituted to maintain continuity and compliance, thereby preventing unauthorized or indefinite retention of sensitive classifications.

out_of_scope.text: This release does not include automated tools or algorithms to determine a contact's Influence Level.
This release will not encompass any external integrations with third-party systems for influence analytics.
No changes will be made to existing user permissions in the CRM system regarding contact detail visibility.

assumptions.text: Users have the knowledge and criteria to manually assess the Influence Level of their contacts based on established protocols.
All users of this CRM have the necessary permissions to edit contact details.
Data integrity is maintained; users will not misuse the Influence Level categorization.

definitions.text: 'Influence Level' means an assigned categorical value (Low, Medium, High) to indicate the importance of a contact in decision-making or project engagement, with specific criteria: 'Low' is for contacts with minimal impact, 'Medium' for contacts that can influence but are not central to decisions, and 'High' for contacts who are critical in decision-making processes.
definitions.note: Definitions of influence levels were clarified with specific criteria to prevent subjective interpretations and ensure consistency.

definitions.text: 'Visual representation' means a graphical or tabular display that allows users to quickly understand the influence status of their contacts at a glance.

success_criteria.text: At least 75% of users report satisfaction with the new contact categorization feature through a follow-up survey conducted one month after release.

tension.summary: The primary disagreement centered around the management of 'Influence Level' data and access permissions. The Proposer and Critic eventually reached a consensus on defining clear roles and procedures to address confidentiality risks, ensuring that only authorized users can modify sensitive categorizations.

proposer.worry: The successful implementation of defined user roles and permissions may be complex and require thorough testing.

critic.worry: The potential for subjective assessments remains, but current revisions significantly mitigate risks.

issues.challenge: The proposal does not specify who can see or modify the 'Influence Level' of contacts, creating a risk that unauthorized users may alter sensitive categorizations, particularly of diplomatic contacts.
issues.failure_scenario: A project manager without proper clearance alters the influence level of a critical diplomatic contact, leading to strategic decisions being made based on incorrect information.
issues.resolution_test: What user roles are permitted to view and modify the 'Influence Level' of contacts?
